item.research_question: What are the microstructure evolution, microhardness, and corrosion behavior of (CoCrFeNi)95Nb5 high-entropy alloy coatings fabricated by plasma spraying on Q235 steel substrates?
item.material_system: (CoCrFeNi)95Nb5 high-entropy alloy coating on Q235 steel substrate
item.processing_route: Vacuum plasma spraying (ZP-2000, DWAUTO) using atomized powder; arc power 30 kW, current 500 A, Ar flow 45 L/min, powder delivery gas 4 L/min, spraying distance 100 mm
item.test_conditions: Microhardness tested at 500 g load for 15 s; electrochemical polarization in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution at 298 K, potential range −0.5 to 0.5 V, scan rate 1 mV/s
key_findings: A new Laves phase formed in the coating compared to the powder, which contained only a simple FCC phase.
Elemental segregation occurred with Cr and Nb enriched in the interdendritic phase, while Co, Fe, and Ni concentrated in the dendritic region.
The transition zone width at the coating-substrate junction was merely 2 μm.
The microhardness of the coating was 321 HV0.5, significantly higher than the substrate's ~122 HV0.5.
The coating exhibited a significantly higher pitting potential and lower passivation current density than other HEA coatings in 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
Selective corrosion occurred where the interdendritic phase rich in Nb and Cr was preferentially corroded as an anode.
Tiny dish-shaped pitting pits with diameters of 1~5 μm were observed only in the gray (interdendritic) phase region.
item.mechanism: The formation of the Laves phase and elemental segregation is attributed to the faster cooling rate of plasma spraying and differences in melting points (Cr: 2133 K, Nb: 2750 K vs. Co: 1770 K, Fe: 1811 K, Ni: 1728 K). The excellent corrosion resistance is due to a dense passivation film containing Cr2O3 and Nb2O5, while selective corrosion occurs because the standard potential of Nb (−1.1 V) and Cr (−0.74 V) is more negative than Fe, Ni, and Co, causing the Cr/Nb-rich interdendritic phase to act as an anode once the film is damaged.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The text does not explicitly state future work.
quotes: The width of transition zone was merely 2 μm.
The microhardness of the (CoCrFeNi)95Nb5 HEA coating was 321 HV0.5, which is significantly higher than that of the substrate.

The pitting potential of the (CoCrFeNi)95Nb5 HEA coating was significantly higher than that of other coatings, which was mainly because of the dense passivation film formed by Cr and Nb on the surface of the coating.
